For this project, when evaluating form validation and email handling work:

**Build and test commands**: The project uses `npm test` (jest), and form changes in src/components/pages/CheckoutPage should extend the existing spec at src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/CheckoutForm.spec.tsx rather than create parallel test files. Changes must pass linting via pre-commit hooks.

**Branch and commit requirements**: The pre-commit hook enforces branch names matching ^(feature|bugfix|tech|release|hotfix)/[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+(/[a-z0-9-]+)?$, and commit messages are validated via commitlint. Any brief that describes committing work on a branch outside these patterns (e.g., main, develop, or custom names) is describing work that will be rejected at the hook and cannot ship.

**Form validation patterns**: This project uses react-hook-form for form state. Email validation logic typically sits in form schemas (joi validators are a dependency) or in component-level validation. Case sensitivity changes must be applied consistently wherever email is validated—both client-side validation and server-side processing (especially payment processing). A brief that handles case normalization only on the client side while accepting mixed-case email server-side is incomplete and will cause production bugs.

**Testing form inputs**: The project has @testing-library/user-event as a dev dependency. Tests should simulate user input (typing mixed-case email) and verify normalization happens, not just check that a field exists. Snapshot tests of form components are fragile; prefer assertion-based tests.

**Payment path sensitivity**: Checkout is payment-critical. Any change to email validation can affect payment processor matching (Stripe is a dependency), order confirmation emails, and receipt matching. A brief that only changes the form component without verifying downstream email handling is incomplete.
